item.content:encoded:
It's one of those cases where I like it although there's a lot I can nitpick about.

For instance, how does he keep managing to speak with a slit throat, tracheal trauma and two gunshot wounds to the head if he doesn't regenrate damage? He shouldn't have the motor capacity to speak even if his body "keeps functionning".

Second, the bit about how other SCPs have regeneraive abilities that feels unnecessary. There's no-one reading this who won't already know that. It kind of feels as if it was put there to say "see? I didn't go for the cliché". I think it would work better to just say that he doesn't have regenerative abilities and leave it at that.

Third, and that one's because I'm a big ancient Egypt nerd, but he really shouldn't have any internal organs to begin with as ancient Egyptians removed every organ except for the heart during mummification.

And true, it's not explicitly said that he was mummified, but if he was buried near a Pharaoh's tomb, there's no way he wouldn't be. I found this mistake epecially disappointing as this detail would have really fit in with the "he should be dead yet somehow remains alive" gimmick.

item.content:encoded:
I really love this idea, but the presentation irks me. Unfortunately, the author seems MIA? So I'm putting my tentative ideas for edits here, as instructed, for mod/admin approval.

To start, I'd like to significantly re-word the article (and slightly re-order it); not re-write it completely, I just think there is a lot of awkward/unclear phrasing. But I'm also asking for permission to change the meaning of some bits:

1) "Living state" and "function" are never defined or described, and have the potential to be weirder than they sound. Ambiguity is great, but not when it's ambiguous which parts and ambiguous.

2) Instead of "subject speaks ancient Egyptian" (which should be clarified before describing anything it's said), I'd link to a log of the researchers trying out several different scholarly translators, trying to find the right ancient dialect, with an "interesting" reaction from the one who finally understands.

3) More showing than telling for descriptions like "constant state of agony"… because that's not very clinical or creepy.

I also think having a Dr. Expunged end with a statement to the effect of "in light of X, taking any serious measures to destroy the subject is no longer a consideration" might 1) amp up the enigma factor and 2) make the dumb suggestions problem moot.

Picture might be a nice addition, too— NOT of a whole mummy. Juuuust enough of…. something.

item.content:encoded:
Mixing SCPs is virtually always "bad" - in fact most of the senior staff take great delight in telling you that the worst case scenario you THOUGHT you had come up with might be the BEST that you could get. For example:

  • We don't understand 138 already. For all we know, he's UNdead. The process could destroy him. This, by the way, is probably the BEST that would happen.
  • Prolonged exposure to 427 results in a "Flesh Beast" - assuming you use a normal person. 138 seems to be unkillable already. This is a BAD combination.
  • 138 was locked away. Some make the mistake of thinking he should be healed. He was stabbed seventeen times. And had his throat cut. Then put in a stone box and hidden from what someone probably thought was all eternity. I'm not too eager to have this guy up and about.

Read the destruction logs of attempts to kill 682. The ones that turn out the WORST are the one where they try to use another SCP to destroy it.

Somewhere there's a story of where they mix five SCPs. I don't remember the name of the story, but it's a very Bright day…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well, the thing is:

A) in-universe cross-testing SCPs can have highly unexpected negative effects, especially when we just don't know how the SCPs work (which is most of them, including 138 and 427).
B) since there is no canon, we can freely assume that 138 and 427 do not exist in the same universes. Or, alternatively, that there's some Big Reason that 138 and 427 can't be cross-tested, but it's just not stated in the article because your clearance isn't high enough to see those articles.
C) There are other in-universe reasons for not trying to de-SCP-ify SCPs. Studying them, for one.

Any of those things can be handwaved into irrelevance with ease, of course, but when the proposal adds nothing from a writing standpoint whatsoever… why, exactly, should they be handwaved?
